contractNotes.finding: `r<ruleId>` is NOT unique across the 7 records: d-line, d-file and e all carry the pinned exemplar id 0123456789abcdef. "One package per record" and "r<ruleId>" cannot both hold.
contractNotes.resolution: The SEMANTIC half (one policy per record) is unambiguous in both the spec and LOWERING.md, so the naming gives: a colliding id takes a `_<specimen>` suffix; a unique id stays exactly on-contract. FLAGGED for the dispatching seat — this is a naming decision, reversible in one place (`packageSuffix`).

contractNotes.finding: The contract does not order the suppression check against the requires check. A match that is BOTH suppressed and requires-satisfied could emit `suppress` or emit nothing.
contractNotes.resolution: MEASURED in the shipped source: all three dispatchers check `requires` FIRST and `continue` before any `onRuleEvent` call — rule-engine.ts:689 (sync regex) before :701, apply-rules-bounded.ts:207 (bounded regex) before :233, rule-engine.ts:1081 (ast-grep) before :1109. The lowering follows the shipped order, so a requires-satisfied match is silent even when the line carries a marker. NOT MEASURED — no fact bundles on disk (`npm run facts` has not run for this record set; run it before reading this note as a reachability claim) — and with nothing measured, this note makes NO claim about differential rows.

contractNotes.finding: The contract's PRECEDING-line marker set is one marker short of the shipped runtime. `isSuppressed` (rule-engine.ts:384-388) routes the preceding line through `hasContextDirective` (:349-356), which accepts `shield-context:` as well as `totem-context:`. The same-line set in the contract is exact (rule-engine.ts:377-381); only the preceding anchor diverges.
contractNotes.resolution: Built to the CONTRACT verbatim — the lowered policies do NOT treat a preceding-line `shield-context:` as suppressing. Widening it to match the runtime would reproduce a semantic LOWERING.md does not state. NOT MEASURED — no fact bundles on disk (`npm run facts` has not run for this record set; run it before reading this note as a reachability claim). FLAGGED for the dispatching seat: this is a one-word amendment to § Lowering 7 if fidelity is wanted.

contractNotes.clause: § Lowering 2 — "Strict always … the host must surface builtin errors as errors"
contractNotes.finding: MEASURED: an OPA WASM module has no `--strict-builtin-errors` equivalent. `opa build -t wasm` accepts a lookahead pattern (exit 0, a 328 KB module); the failure surfaces only at EVAL, as an UNDEFINED rule — the entrypoint returns `[]` with no trap and no `opa_abort`.
contractNotes.resolution: Strictness is made STRUCTURAL in the lowering instead: every emitted pattern is exercised by `patterns_compile` inside the COMPLETE `result` rule, so a compile failure leaves `result` undefined and the host reads an empty result SET as an ERROR ROW. Recorded as a first-order ABI finding, not worked around silently.
